## Declarations and implementations

    // (1/2) * n * R^2 * sin(2*pi/n): the n isosceles triangles from the centre.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regular_polygon#Area
    Area(g: RegularPolygon): Number
        => 0.5 * g.SideCount.ToNumber * g.CircumRadius.Square
        * (1.0 / g.SideCount.ToNumber).Turns.Sin;

    // 2 * n * R * sin(pi/n): the n equal chords of the circumscribed circle.
    Perimeter(g: RegularPolygon): Number
        => 2.0 * g.SideCount.ToNumber * g.CircumRadius
        * (0.5 / g.SideCount.ToNumber).Turns.Sin;


    // TIGHT: the bounds of the computed vertices. (The circumscribed circle's box
    // would be conservative whenever no vertex lands on an axis.)
    Bounds(g: RegularPolygon): Bounds2D
        => g.RegularPolygonVertices.BoundsOfPoints;

    // Even-odd containment over the computed vertex ring.
    Contains(g: RegularPolygon, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => g.RegularPolygonVertices.PolygonContainsPoint(point);

    // The vertex farthest along `direction`. Correct because the polygon is convex,
    // so its support point is always a vertex.
    Support(g: RegularPolygon, direction: Direction2D): Point2D
    {
        var vertices = g.RegularPolygonVertices;
        return vertices.Reduce(vertices.First, (best, v) =>
            direction.Vector.Dot(v.PositionVector) > direction.Vector.Dot(best.PositionVector)
                ? v : best);
    }

    //==
    // # Disk, annulus, sector, segment, and stadium bodies
    //
    // Area, perimeter, bounds, centroid, containment, nearest-point and support bodies
    // for the types declared in `planar.types.plato`.
    //
    // Conventions fixed here:
    //
    //   * PLACED, not origin-centred. Every shape carries its own Center / endpoints; no
    //     body assumes the origin.
    //   * `Area` is non-negative for EVERY type here.
    //   * CONTAINMENT is boundary-INCLUSIVE: every test is an inequality on a distance
    //     or a coordinate (interface doc: "for closed shapes the boundary counts as
    //     inside").
    //   * `ClosestPoint` on a filled REGION returns the query point itself when the
    //     query is contained, which `INearestPoint2D` explicitly permits ("for a region
    //     it may be an interior point").
    //   * ANGLES are `Angle` throughout; `Number` fractions of a turn are converted with
    //     `.Turns` (`angles.library.plato`) rather than by multiplying by pi.
    //
    // Shared kernels live in `geometry.library.plato` and the local-frame
    // helpers in `lines.library.plato`; neither is respelled here.

    //==
    // # Circle
    //
    // The disk region. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle

    // pi * r^2.
    Area(c: Circle): Number
        => Number.Pi * c.Radius.Square;

    // The circumference 2 * pi * r.
    Perimeter(c: Circle): Number
        => 2.0 * Number.Pi * c.Radius;


    // The square of side 2r about the centre.
    Bounds(c: Circle): Bounds2D
        => CenteredBounds(c.Center, c.Radius, c.Radius);

    // True when the point is within Radius of the centre. Boundary inclusive;
    // compares squared distances so no square root is taken.
    Contains(c: Circle, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => c.Center.Between(point).MagnitudeSquared <= c.Radius.Square;

    // The query point when it lies in the disk, otherwise its radial projection
    // onto the circle.
    ClosestPoint(c: Circle, point: Point2D): Point2D
        => c.Contains(point)
        ? point
        : c.Center + c.Center.Between(point).Normalize * c.Radius;

    // The point of the circle farthest along `direction`.
    Support(c: Circle, direction: Direction2D): Point2D
        => c.Center + direction.Vector * c.Radius;

    //==
    // # Annulus
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annulus_(mathematics)

    // pi * (R^2 - r^2).
    Area(a: Annulus): Number
        => Number.Pi * (a.OuterRadius.Square - a.InnerRadius.Square);

    // The TOTAL boundary length: both bounding circles, since the annulus has two
    // boundary components. 2*pi*(R + r).
    Perimeter(a: Annulus): Number
        => 2.0 * Number.Pi * (a.OuterRadius + a.InnerRadius);


    // The bounds of the outer circle.
    Bounds(a: Annulus): Bounds2D
        => CenteredBounds(a.Center, a.OuterRadius, a.OuterRadius);

    // True when the point's distance from the centre lies in [InnerRadius,
    // OuterRadius]. Both boundaries inclusive.
    Contains(a: Annulus, point: Point2D): Boolean
    {
        var distanceSquared = a.Center.Between(point).MagnitudeSquared;
        return distanceSquared >= a.InnerRadius.Square
            && distanceSquared <= a.OuterRadius.Square;
    }

    //==
    // # CircularSector
    //
    // A pie slice. Precondition throughout: Sweep is stored forward and spans at
    // most one full turn. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circular_sector

    // Half the bisector direction of the sweep, as a unit displacement.
    SweepBisector(sweep: AngleInterval): Vector2D
    {
        var mid = sweep.Start + sweep.Extent * 0.5;
        return (mid.Cos, mid.Sin);
    }

    // (1/2) * r^2 * theta, with theta the swept angle in radians.
    Area(s: CircularSector): Number
        => 0.5 * s.Circle.Radius.Square * s.Sweep.Extent.Radians;

    // The arc r*theta plus the two bounding radii.
    Perimeter(s: CircularSector): Number
        => s.Circle.Radius * s.Sweep.Extent.Radians + 2.0 * s.Circle.Radius;

    // On the bisector, at 2/3 * r * sin(alpha)/alpha from the circle's centre,
    // where alpha is the HALF angle — written here with theta = 2*alpha as
    // 4*r*sin(theta/2) / (3*theta). Degenerates to the centre for a zero sweep.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circular_sector#Centroid
    Centroid(s: CircularSector): Point2D
    {
        var theta = s.Sweep.Extent;
        var distance = theta.Radians == 0.0
            ? 0.0
            : 4.0 * s.Circle.Radius * (theta * 0.5).Sin / (3.0 * theta.Radians);
        return s.Circle.Center + SweepBisector(s.Sweep) * distance;
    }

    // CONSERVATIVE, not tight: the bounds of the whole circle. A tight box needs to
    // know which of the four axis extremes the arc actually reaches, which is a
    // four-way angular-interval test this library does not attempt.
    // TODO(content): tighten to the arc's own extremes.
    Bounds(s: CircularSector): Bounds2D
        => s.Circle.Bounds;
